summary: Submitted an experiment request for the startup committed-log replay investigation. The new harness, exp_restore_midband_test.go, runs three restarts of retained single-node cluster state with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and the default MaxAppendEntries of 64, where each cluster commits 200 commands, snapshots, commits a second batch and shuts down, so only the post-snapshot tail is replayed. Local verification shows a 50-batch tail (3198 entries) returns in 1 ms, a 128-batch tail (8192 entries, exactly the fsmMutateCh capacity) returns in 3 ms, and 129 batches (8194 entries) does not return within 20 s with one goroutine parked in processLogs. This fills the account's stated gap that no real prefix had been restarted with a tail between 5 and 129 batches, and it brackets the capacity boundary on cluster-produced state with the tail held fixed to a single entry, so the trigger can no longer be attributed to replay volume or slowness. The request anchors prerequisites on the three case events and asserts returned == true on each result event; it validates against submission.schema.json.
